claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks meaningful progression, providing high-end supercars and rewards too easily from the start.

citations.review_text:
As much as it is fun to casually just drive around the map with a wheel Forza Horizon 5 feels boring and like a chore to play.

Progression doesn't exist. You turn the wheel? EXP. You stare at a tree? EXP. You fart? The game aggressively throws three Bugattis and a million credits at your face.

The map is beautiful but roads are just suggestions. You can just tape down the throttle and bulldoze straight through the entire ecosystem at 200 mph.

You spend two hours in the garage tuning your absolute dream car. You pull up to the starting line, pumped and ready to unleash hell. The game: "Ah, excuse me, no. This is a 'Sensible Footwear' event. You are strictly required to drive a factory-standard 2014 Ford Focus."
I get that restrictions exist to make races fair but in a sandbox game supposedly built around limitless freedom, nothing hurts more than the game confiscating your custom built monster and forcing you to drive a commuter hatchback.

The menu is so cluttered with promotion and nonsense it takes 10 minutes to navigate an unholy labyrinth of pop-up ads, seasonal promos and wheelspins just to find your garage and change a tire. This game is expensive and I don't feel like I got even close to money worth from this game.

This was a game gifted to me by a guy I know who obtains these kinds of games. I haven't played it long, but it's long enough that I feel like I should write a review for it.

[h1]The Open World Experience[/h1]
First of all, I have never played the Forza series before. I know it's been out for a while now, but I just never got into it. What I'm used to, as far as racing games go, are games where you just go through menus and start races - things like Asphalt Legends (previously Asphalt 9 Legends), Mario Kart, F-ZERO - you know, those type games. Some have challenges not strictly about racing, true, but they don't typically allow you to explore a vast world within their games.

Forza is different. I could practically drive forever - in fact, just for fun, I even tried to climb a mountain with my Ford Bronco! I wasn't in a race or anything - just exploring the open world map. It's nice to have that casual approach to a game that could've been nothing but races.

Of course, there are the races, and there's some challenges like taking photos with your car and certain scenery, but just being able to drive without doing anything is pretty sweet.

[h1]Customization Out The Wazoo[/h1]
[b]DANG![/b] I can customize soooo much! I have gained a variety of cars already, thanks to the bundle I was gifted, plus I have been earning more through just playing games.

Each and every car can be customized and tuned - down to the finest details! Brakes, shocks, engine, tires, hood, wings, frame, windows - you name it, it can be customized with colors, upgrades, and decals! I can even adjust the levels for shifting gears, PSI of tires, and more via upgrades. TBH, it feels like playing Asphalt Legends again... which is both a good and a bad thing, but we'll get to the questionable stuff later.

As for character customization? ...Meh. It's about as much as I expected. Can't really make the character look like me, and it's basically so I can have a bunch of cosmetics and cloth…

[h1]Forza Horizon 5: A masterpiece that’s always there for you[/h1]

Forza Horizon 5 is more than just a racing game; it’s an absolute [b]masterpiece[/b]. What I love most is how it fits literally any mood. Whether you're feeling down, stressed, or just pure joy — this game takes you as you are. You can just hop in, start driving, and let the world wash over you. It’s like a digital comfort zone.

[h2]Mexico & The Vibe[/h2]
Setting the game in Mexico was such a [u]perfect call[/u]. The map is incredibly immersive and just beautiful to look at. And man, the music... the main menu theme alone is something I could listen to for hours. It sets the vibe perfectly before you even turn the key.

You can really tell the devs poured their hearts into the technical side:
[list]
    [*][b]Engine Sounds:[/b] Each of the [b]900+ cars[/b] sounds unique. I love how the exhaust note changes depending on your surroundings — the way it echoes when you blast through a tunnel is just spot on.

[/list]

In a vacuum, this is a *great* racing game. Unfortunately for Forza Horizon 5, it doesn't exist in a vacuum; it exists alongside other Forza Horizon games. The only timeframe where this game became reasonably good was between December 15, 2024 (with the delisting of Forza Horizon 4), and May 16, 2026 (with the release of Forza Horizon 6).
Between those two games in the series, I struggle to think of a single thing that Forza Horizon 5 actually did better. Sure, the cars look and sound great, but this game is just missing the *soul* that other games in the series have had. I'm willing to extend a lot of grace to Playground Games, what with this game being developed during a global pandemic and all, but at some point you have to draw a line in the sand and recognize that this entry just does not live up to the standards set by the series.
For starters, the music. Now, I realize that this is purely subjective on my part, but I feel like FH5 is sorely lacking in the soundtrack department. Every song felt middling at best, and failed to capture the energy of Horizon Mexico other than a couple of Spanish covers of pop songs. I also understand that people are divided on the in-game DJs, but if it weren't for the iconic energy brought by Scott Tyler and Amy Simpson, I would have very little reason to listen to radio at all (skill songs not withstanding).
Secondly, as other have pointed out, progression is completely non-existent in this game. I'm not going to beat the dead horse found in dozens of other comments, but suffice it to say that building out the festival via accolades did not feel the least bit meaningful. To make matters worse, accolades become nearly pointless after completing the festival aside from being used as a ranking metric among clans.
But finally, and perhaps most egregiously, was the controversial opinion to finally make your character have voice lines. Now look, I know there are running jokes about silent protagonists from dozens of other game series…

A huge sandbox where the devs throw free cars at you and overwhelm you with things to do. If you stick with it though, it can be really fun. Especially for people who like arcade racing (but you can tweak settings to make it more sim-like), achievements, or collecting cars. The sense of speed, the sound design, and the visuals are all amazing. There's something in this sandbox for every type of driver: rally, drift, drag racing, road racing, street racing, stunt jumpers and speed freaks.

HOWEVER, it cannot be overstated that the actual narrative / story elements are horrendous. No personality, no soul. Feels like every line of dialogue was focus-grouped and strategically written to be as mild and inoffensive as possible. And the cutscenes can't be skipped...! It's soul-crushing and draining.

Overall, I think Forza Horizon is a really enjoyable game that can keep you entertained for a very long time. The cars feel fantastic to drive, and the individual races are a lot of fun — especially the off-road tracks, where you can really feel the terrain. The selection of cars is also huge, and there are plenty of customization options. The game world is varied (forests, deserts, mountains, cities, etc.) and fun to explore.

However, there are also a few downsides, which I’d like to list below:

1) The requirement to have a Microsoft account, the unnecessary and out-of-place casino-style wheel-spin UI when winning new cars, and the challenge cards prominently displayed on the map that cannot be hidden — which are not part of the base game (and must therefore be purchased first) — really rubbed me the wrong way.
2) The constant chatter of the unlikable characters against an overly colorful backdrop sometimes makes the game world feel pretty generic. As for the radio stations, I often wished there were more customization options because the music selection just wasn’t really my thing. I often preferred to just turn the radio off.
3) As much fun as it is to drive around, the game really should have a free fast-travel option on a map this big. And when it comes to starting a race, you still have to sit through several layers of loading and cutscenes that I really wish I could skip more often.
4) The game constantly tries to push you toward certain activities (for example by repeatedly opening the mission map), even though the game is supposed to be all about player freedom. Some level of guidance is fine, but this kind of constant nudging really got on my nerves.
5) There was no German voiceover for the Donut missions. There’s also a strange vehicle-related glitch that I couldn’t explain. I'm not really sure how to start talking about this game.
I guess I'll start by saying that the only Forza games I've played are Horizon 1 and 5. I emulated 1, and then jumped to 5 because it was the only one on steam (sidenote, delisting games is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). Maybe my opinion of this game would be less favorable had I played 2-4 first, because the biggest complaint I hear about 5 is that it doesn't make any meaningful improvements to the formula. It's just the same thing again with a new coat of paint, except it does some things worse than previous games. This could be 100% true. Hell, there are some things that I think Horizon 1 does better, like your progression through the festival and the general vibe. 5 feels very sanitized and simplified. You start at the top, you're showered with rewards, everyone calls you "superstar" constantly and feel like they're only there to hype you up. None of the attitude of the rivals in 1. Races are open to all performance classes and car types, so the game never pushes you to try new things. There's no sense of working your way towards anything; you just kinda pick whatever events you feel like doing until the whole festival is unlocked. It didn't help that I got the deluxe edition, so the game gave me a ton of high performance cars before I even did anything. I would even argue that the soundtrack in 1 is better, even though there are some bangers in 5.
But with all that said, I did still put 200 hours into the game, so clearly they did SOMETHING right. I think what I've concluded is that while it may not have any standout features, it isn't really bad at any of the things you can do. Racing is still fun. Cars control very nicely, and there's a large selection of cool cars to get. Taking a drive around the map is very nice. EventLab is full of cool ♥♥♥♥ that other people have made. I don't know, it's just fun. It's kinda become my comfort game.
So if you're a diehard forza fan, I totally see how it could be disappointing. But …

I also don't like the progression system in the Forza Horizon games. You're constantly spammed with notifications, rewards, achievements, and collectibles, to the point where they lose their value. Instead of feeling rewarding, it just becomes overwhelming and feels like filler.

[h1]15.6 RPM / 20[/h1]

I don’t think this is the strongest entry in the series, but I don’t think this is the worst either.

Overall I would say it’s worth playing, it is a lot of fun and has a lot to offer. I think the main thing the game fails to do is it has a weak progression system. It almost gives you too much freedom to do whatever you want and some people might prefer this, but there is a lot of other good content in the game that might get overlooked if players get bored before coming across it all. It doesn’t help that some of the races are a little merh, nothing too exciting, and can feel a little repetitive at times.

The map is really good, i’d go as far and say it’s up there as one of the better locations they have done the series in. It’s interactive and beautiful and quite dense. Slightly smaller but more filled than some other entries which I personally prefer.

The off-road races just hit different, it seems like they nailed it in this game and they do shine in comparison to the other races.

Both DLC expansions are fantastic and absolutely carry the game. I would highly recommend getting the game for the DLCs alone. Truly great maps, races, vehicles and content. Can’t fault them at all. Also the “stories” missions are really good as well, some nostalgia in there and generally really fun.

Forza Horizon 5 is easily the best racing game I’ve played. I originally picked it up as something casual to play between bigger, story-driven games, but it quickly became one of the games I spent the most time with.

What surprised me the most was the sheer amount of content. There’s always something to do, whether it’s racing, exploring, collecting cars, or just driving around. More importantly, the content feels varied and well-made rather than being there just for the sake of quantity.

My only real criticism is the progression and reward system. The game is extremely generous, to the point where you’ll end up with a huge collection of cars almost immediately. Before you have time to appreciate one car, you’ve already unlocked several more. While it’s fun at first, it made the cars feel less special and took away some of the sense of progression that I usually enjoy in racing games.

Even with that flaw, Forza Horizon 5 is an incredible experience and a game I kept coming back to for hundreds of hours.
